data.name: Privacy_Statement
data.value: GameRadar has no server: it collects, transmits and sells no data. Your history, your settings and its caches stay on this computer; your Xbox session, your Steam key, your PlayStation token and your Epic sign-in are encrypted there by Windows; the EA token is never saved. The error log, free of any secret, only leaves this computer if you send it yourself.

data.name: Privacy_Services
data.value: The app only contacts the services it needs: Microsoft (Xbox Live, Game Pass catalog and Microsoft Store), Steam (your history, achievements and wishlist if you connect your account, and its games given away and free weekends on the "Free games" page, without an account), Sony (PlayStation Network if you connect it, the PS Plus catalog if you chose a PS Plus plan, the PlayStation Store when you search for a game to add and for its top sellers if the "PlayStation Store" box is ticked, and the PS Plus catalog then if the PlayStation Store does not answer, and the PS Plus games of the month on the "Free games" page if you chose a plan), GOG (your public profile if you enter it, and the catalog of its best sellers, without an account), EA (the games you played in the EA app, only when you paste the EA page), Epic Games (your games, play time and achievements if you connect your account, and the top sellers, most played and top rated of its catalog as well as its games given away this week, without an account), Amazon (the games given to Prime members, on the "Free games" page, without an account), and GitHub to check for updates. Each one only receives what it needs to answer: your sign-in to read your own data, nothing personal for the catalogs.
